challenge.better_approach: Raising the reseal door's default budget would hide every slow proof at once; the budget is the proof's own byte (8383a32d20c5), so one declaration is the smaller change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That 137 s is stable on Linux: two measurements (137, 133) agree within 3%. Windows is unmeasured and named as such in the how.

answers.falsifier: the census proof source declares PROOF_TIMEOUT_S as a top-level positive integer, 300, read through the tester's declared_timeout (None today, so this tooth is red before the build); run_proof on a fixture carrying the census proof's declared value, at the reseal door's 120 s caller budget, records a run budget of 300, not 120
answers.from_idea: none, because it is the budget debt cf32e6f141e0 fixed for another proof, measured on cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_a_census_names_every_outside_reader.py
answers.how: Add a top-level `PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 300` to cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_a_census_names_every_outside_reader.py. Budget = measured wall plus margin: 300 s is 2.2x the 137 s Linux wall and 2.5x the 120 s default that times it out. No Windows wall is read; if one measures above 300 s the number is re-measured, not guessed up. The mechanism is 8383a32d20c5's; the proof copies cf32e6f141e0's test_the_scratch_proof_declares_a_budget_above_its_wall, whose first tooth reds an undeclared proof because declared_timeout returns None.
answers.traces_to: Law 9 (green is earned: a proof timed out stales a component it never judged) and Law 3 (the budget follows the measured wall)
answers.what: The outside-readers census proof declares its own time limit above its measured wall, so a reseal that touches artifact.py runs it to a verdict instead of timing it out and staling the artifact component.

bullets.text: The cf32 pattern's first tooth (declared_timeout == N) already reds an undeclared proof, since declared_timeout returns None for one.
